unit.title: Goals and limits: a model, linear programming in 2D

lesson.title: Draw the plans that fit
lesson.subtitle: Lines, a shaded shape and the best corner

video.title: Draw the plans that fit
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — your maths teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talks to the student)

scenes.visual: Ms Salma at the garden fence with a clipboard of graph paper; pupils with watering cans behind her.
scenes.animation: Tomato and bean signs pop up; a pencil starts drawing axes.
scenes.narration: This year your class runs the school garden. Tomato beds earn thirty coins, bean beds forty. But land, water and your own hours are limited. Where is the best plan? Let’s draw it.

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: draw the plans that fit, and find the best one.

scenes.visual: Three limits type out on a card, each beside an icon: land, water, hours.
scenes.animation: Each line types in as it is said.
scenes.narration: Call the tomato beds x and the bean beds y. Land: x plus y is at most eight. Water: two x plus y is at most fourteen cans a day. Your hours: x plus three y is at most eighteen a week.

scenes.visual: Axes appear; the land line joins 8 on each axis; the area below it shades lightly.
scenes.animation: The line draws itself; the shade spreads down.
scenes.narration: On graph paper, each limit is a straight line. For land, mark eight on each axis and join them. Plans on the line use all the land. Plans below it fit.

scenes.visual: The water and hours lines join the land line; a five-sided shape shades; its five corners ring.
scenes.animation: Lines draw in turn; the shape fills; rings pop.
scenes.narration: Draw all three lines, and shade where all three are kept. That shape holds every plan that fits. Its corners are where the lines meet.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma points at the land line on a big graph. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! On the graph, which side of the land line holds the plans that fit?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets a check; the region below the land line glows; a dot on the line blinks.
scenes.animation: The check pops; the shade pulses.
scenes.narration: Below the line, towards zero: there, x plus y is less than eight. Points on the line fit too: they use all the land exactly.

scenes.visual: A dashed line crosses the shape low down, then glides up, parallel, until it touches one corner.
scenes.animation: The dashed line slides up in steps; a profit counter rises.
scenes.narration: Now the goal. All plans with the same profit lie on one straight line. Slide that line up, and the profit grows. The last point of the shape it touches is the best plan.

scenes.visual: The dashed line rests on one corner; a star lands there with 290.
scenes.narration: Here, that’s the corner three tomato beds and five bean beds: two hundred and ninety coins. The best plan is always at a corner. That’s linear programming: straight-line limits and a straight-line goal.

scenes.visual: Three gauges: land full, hours full, water with a small gap.
scenes.animation: Gauges fill; the water gauge stops short.
scenes.narration: At the best corner, two limits are used up: the land, eight beds, and your hours, eighteen. Water has three cans to spare. So more water wouldn’t help, but more hours would.

scenes.visual: A rota on the wall: the same two names in every slot, then the names spread across the whole class.
scenes.animation: Names shuffle out across the rota.
scenes.narration: But who does the work? A bean bed takes three of your hours a week. If the same few pupils always do the watering, the plan isn’t fair, however much it earns. Share the hours, and write that into the plan.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: the shaded garden plans, a dashed line, sliders.
scenes.animation: A finger drags a slider; then taps inside the shape.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: The best plan is at a corner
scenes.narration: In the app, drag the profit to aim for up, slowly, and watch the last corner it touches. Then tap inside the shape to try a plan of your own.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor holds a new price tag: tomatoes 50. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Tomatoes now sell for fifty coins a bed. Does the best corner change?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets the check; four summary lines and a takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Yes: the best plan moves to six tomato beds and two bean beds, three hundred and eighty coins. Remember: each limit is a line, the plans that fit are the shaded shape, and the best plan is at a corner. Change a price or a limit, and check the corners again.

scenes.visual: A pupil’s graph paper: three lines, the shape shaded, corners circled with profits.
scenes.animation: Corners get circled one by one; one gets a star.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: draw the garden on graph paper. Shade the plans that fit, mark the five corners, and work out the profit at each. Which corner wins?

checkpoints.prompt: Which side of the land line holds the plans that fit?

options.text: Above the line, away from zero
Only the points on the line

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — below the line x + y is less than 8, so those plans fit; the line itself fits too.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — above the line x + y is more than 8 beds. The plans that fit are below it, towards zero, and on it.

checkpoints.prompt: Tomatoes now sell for 50 coins a bed. Does the best corner change?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — at 50 coins the profit line tilts, and (6, 2) earns 380, the most.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the shape is the same, but the profit line tilts. Now (6, 2) earns 380, more than (3, 5)’s 350.
